sections.notes: §4.3.2.1 Transfer family: arriving and departing control-transfer clauses, nested conditions, and supporting note. Parent + mutually-exclusive sibling shape (a/b).
ICAO Doc 4444 §4.3.1 General: ATS authority designation of ATC unit and working-position responsibility. Hardened in clearance_comms_2026-04-30.
ICAO Doc 4444 §§4.3.3-4.3.5: approach/area and sector responsibility transfer rules. Hardened in clearance_comms_2026-04-30.
§4.5.7.5 Readback family: parent clause, subordinate list (a/b/c), notes, and following standalone clauses (4.5.7.5.1.1, 4.5.7.5.2, 4.5.7.5.2.1).
ICAO Doc 4444 §§4.5.1-4.5.7.4: clearance scope, purpose, timing, contents, clearance limit, route, level, and amended-clearance semantics. Hardened in clearance_comms_2026-04-30.

§7.9 Control of Departing Aircraft: §7.9.1 Departure sequence (with priority factors a-f), §7.9.2 Separation of departing aircraft (the 'crossed end of runway / started a turn' rule), §7.9.3.1-7.9.3.5 Take-off clearance (timing, ATC clearance prerequisite, TAKE-OFF phraseology rule, 'immediate take-off' clearance). Includes inline Note text and figure-layout artifacts.

§7.10 Control of Arriving Aircraft: §7.10.1 Separation of landing aircraft (mirrors §7.9.2), §7.10.2 Clearance to land timing/runway-designator rule, §7.10.3 Landing and roll-out manoeuvres (a-d list of optional instructions, HEAVY aircraft constraint, vacate-report rule).

§4.6.1 General Horizontal Speed Control Instructions: §4.6.1.1-7. Speed-control issuance, persistence-on-pilot-side, holding-pattern exclusion, frequency-of-changes, comply-or-inform, Mach/IAS units convention, cancellation rule. Includes inline Notes about fuel/configuration considerations.

§5.8.1-5.8.4 Wake turbulence longitudinal separation minima: §5.8.1 Applicability, §5.8.2 Arriving aircraft, §5.8.3 Departing aircraft (parallel/displaced/opposite-direction scenarios), §5.8.4 Displaced landing threshold. Heavy regulatory text with category tables.

§7.11.1-7.11.6 Reduced runway separation minima between aircraft using the same runway: safety-assessment prerequisite, hours-of-daylight constraint, aircraft classification, departing-vs-landing exclusion, conditional preconditions list.

§7.6.1-7.6.3.1.1 Control of Aerodrome Traffic: §7.6.1 General clarity-of-instructions duty, §7.6.2 Designated positions of aircraft (positions 1-6 with associated controller actions), §7.6.3.1 Traffic on the manoeuvring area, §7.6.3.1.1 Taxi clearance content rules. Includes inline figure-layout artifacts.
ICAO Doc 4444 §§4.11.1-4.11.3: position-report timing, voice-report contents, and initial call content after channel change. Hardened in clearance_comms_2026-04-30.
ICAO Doc 4444 §4.14: ATC unit reporting of communication, navigation, surveillance, or other safety-significant system failures. Hardened in clearance_comms_2026-04-30.

ICAO Doc 4444 §12.3.1.4: transfer of control/frequency-change phraseologies. Manifest authority ceiling is operational_guidance because this seam uses the window as phraseology support. Hardened in clearance_comms_2026-04-30.

sourceUnits.claimText: Prior to issuing a taxi clearance, the controller shall determine where the aircraft concerned is parked.
sourceUnits.rationale: Direct authoritative requirement from 7.6.3.1.1.1. Consistent across all attempts.
exactSourceQuotes: Prior to issuing a taxi clearance, the controller shall determine where the aircraft concerned is parked.

sourceUnits.claimText: Position 4 is a normal point for issuing clearance to land when practicable.
sourceUnits.rationale: Corrected replacement for a rejected over-promoted Position 4 record. The source describes a normal clearance position, not a shall-strength issuance duty.
exactSourceQuotes:
The following positions of aircraft in the traffic and taxi circuits are the positions where aircraft normally receive
aerodrome control tower clearances.
Position 4. Clearance to land is issued here as practicable.

curationApplied.reasoning: Adds the source-supported Position 4 fact with corrected descriptive wording after the original shall-strength candidate was rejected.

sourceUnits.claimText: Position 5 is a normal point for issuing clearance to taxi to apron.
sourceUnits.rationale: Corrected replacement for a rejected over-promoted Position 5 record. The source describes normal aerodrome-control positions; the corrected claim keeps that descriptive force.
exactSourceQuotes:
The following positions of aircraft in the traffic and taxi circuits are the positions where aircraft normally receive
aerodrome control tower clearances.
Position 5. Clearance to taxi to apron is issued here.

curationApplied.reasoning: Adds the source-supported Position 5 fact with corrected descriptive wording after the original shall-strength candidate was rejected.

sourceUnits.claimText: Parking information shall be issued at Position 6 if necessary.
sourceUnits.rationale: Attempt 1 uniquely decomposed Position 6. Defines parking information issuance.
exactSourceQuotes: Position 6. Parking information issued here, if necessary.

sourceUnits.claimText: At Position 2, if there is conflicting traffic, the departing aircraft will be held at this position. Engine run-up will, when required, normally be performed here.
sourceUnits.rationale: Attempt 1 uniquely decomposed Position 2. Defines holding and run-up procedures.
exactSourceQuotes: Position 2. If there is conflicting traffic, the departing aircraft will be held at this position. Engine run-up will, when required, normally be performed here.

curationApplied.reasoning: The quoted Position 2 text exists verbatim and supports the claim text, but it uses “will” and “normally,” not shall/must wording. The correct fix is to downgrade the modality from shall to none and lower the authority class from authoritative_requirement to operational_guidance rather than treating it as a binding requirement.

sourceUnits.claimText: The controller shall ensure that instructions and information which require the flight crew to employ visual detection, recognition and observation are phrased in a clear, concise and complete manner.
sourceUnits.rationale: Direct authoritative requirement from 7.6.1. Consistent across all attempts.
exactSourceQuotes: the controller shall ensure that instructions and information which require the flight crew to employ visual detection, recognition and observation are phrased in a clear, concise and complete manner.

sourceUnits.claimText: Where standard taxi routes have not been published, a taxi route should, whenever possible, be described by use of taxiway and runway designators. Other relevant information, such as an aircraft to follow or give way to, shall also be provided to a taxiing aircraft.
sourceUnits.rationale: Mixed modality clause. The description method is 'should', but the provision of other relevant info is 'shall'. The claim captures the full obligation. Consistent across all attempts.
exactSourceQuotes: Where standard taxi routes have not been published, a taxi route should, whenever possible, be described by use of taxiway and runway designators. Other relevant information, such as an aircraft to follow or give way to, shall also be provided to a taxiing aircraft.

sourceUnits.claimText: Where practicable, all clearances should be issued without waiting for aircraft to initiate the call.
sourceUnits.rationale: Operational guidance using 'should' and 'practicable'. Consistent across all attempts.
exactSourceQuotes: Where practicable, all clearances should be issued without waiting for aircraft to initiate the call.

sourceUnits.claimText: When a taxi clearance contains a taxi limit beyond a runway, it shall contain an explicit clearance to cross or an instruction to hold short of that runway.
sourceUnits.rationale: Direct authoritative requirement from 7.6.3.1.1.2. Consistent across all attempts.
exactSourceQuotes: When a taxi clearance contains a taxi limit beyond a runway, it shall contain an explicit clearance to cross or an instruction to hold short of that runway.

sourceUnits.claimText: The appropriate ATS authority should whenever practicable publish in the national AIP standard taxi routes to be used at an aerodrome. Standard taxi routes should be identified by appropriate designators and should be used in taxi clearances.
sourceUnits.rationale: Operational guidance using 'should'. Consistent across all attempts. Marked advisory_only.
exactSourceQuotes: The appropriate ATS authority should whenever practicable publish in the national AIP standard taxi routes to be used at an aerodrome. Standard taxi routes should be identified by appropriate designators and should be used in taxi clearances.

curationApplied.reasoning: The claim is a verbatim match to the source, uses the correct 'should' modality, and is appropriately classified as non-authoritative best-practice guidance. It is not redundant with the accepted siblings, which cover adjacent taxi-clearance provisions rather than publication and use of standard taxi routes.

sourceUnits.claimText: Position 3 is a normal point for issuing take-off clearance when issuing it at Position 2 is not practicable.
sourceUnits.rationale: Corrected replacement for a rejected over-promoted Position 3 record. The source describes normal aerodrome-control positions; it does not state a shall-strength obligation.
exactSourceQuotes:
The following positions of aircraft in the traffic and taxi circuits are the positions where aircraft normally receive
aerodrome control tower clearances.
Position 3. Take-off clearance is issued here, if not practicable at position 2.

curationApplied.reasoning: Adds the source-supported Position 3 fact with corrected non-mandatory wording after the original shall-strength candidate was rightly rejected.

sourceUnits.claimText: At Position 1, runway-in-use information and taxi clearances shall be given.
sourceUnits.rationale: Attempt 1 uniquely decomposed Position 1 into a specific requirement for runway-in-use info and taxi clearances. This is a standard ICAO phraseology requirement at this position.
exactSourceQuotes: Position 1. Aircraft initiates call to taxi for departing flight. Runway-in-use information and taxi clearances given.

sourceUnits.claimText: Aircraft should be watched closely as they approach these positions so that proper clearances may be issued without delay.
sourceUnits.rationale: Operational guidance using 'should'. Consistent across all attempts.
exactSourceQuotes: Aircraft should be watched closely as they approach these positions so that proper clearances may be issued without delay.

sourceUnits.claimText: Arriving aircraft executing an instrument approach procedure will normally enter the traffic circuit on final except when visual manoeuvring to the landing runway is required.
sourceUnits.rationale: Note 1 provides background context on normal procedures. Not a direct controller obligation. Marked support_only.
exactSourceQuotes: Note 1.— Arriving aircraft executing an instrument approach procedure will normally enter the traffic circuit on final except when visual manoeuvring to the landing runway is required.

curationApplied.reasoning: The quote exists verbatim in the source, the claim accurately reflects the note, and the note/background_support classification is floor-consistent. It is non-normative background material, but it is self-contained and not redundant with the accepted sibling candidates.

sourceUnits.claimText: Taxi clearances shall contain concise instructions and adequate information so as to assist the flight crew to follow the correct taxi routes, to avoid collision with other aircraft or objects and to minimize the potential for the aircraft inadvertently entering an active runway.
sourceUnits.rationale: Direct authoritative requirement from 7.6.3.1.1.1. Consistent across all attempts.
exactSourceQuotes: Taxi clearances shall contain concise instructions and adequate information so as to assist the flight crew to follow the correct taxi routes, to avoid collision with other aircraft or objects and to minimize the potential for the aircraft inadvertently entering an active runway.

sourceUnits.claimText: An aircraft may be cleared to land when there is reasonable assurance that the separation in 7.10.1, or prescribed in accordance with 7.11 will exist when the aircraft crosses the runway threshold.
sourceUnits.rationale: Condition for clearance. Attempt 1 split this into timing/designator, but the condition itself is a distinct requirement present in all attempts implicitly or explicitly.
exactSourceQuotes: An aircraft may be cleared to land when there is reasonable assurance that the separation in 7.10.1, or prescribed in accordance with 7.11 will exist when the aircraft crosses the runway threshold

sourceUnits.claimText: A landing aircraft may be requested to vacate the runway at a specified exit taxiway.
sourceUnits.rationale: Optional instruction type. Consistent across all attempts.
exactSourceQuotes: c) vacate the runway at a specified exit taxiway;

sourceUnits.claimText: If the pilot-in-command considers that he or she is unable to comply with the requested operation, the controller shall be advised without delay.
sourceUnits.rationale: Pilot reporting obligation. Consistent across all attempts.
exactSourceQuotes: If the pilot-in-command considers that he or she is unable to comply with the requested operation, the controller shall be advised without delay.

sourceUnits.rationale: Optional instruction type. Consistent across all attempts.
exactSourceQuotes: d) expedite vacating the runway.

sourceUnits.claimText: The landing clearance shall include the designator of the landing runway.
sourceUnits.rationale: Phraseology requirement. Consistent across all attempts.
exactSourceQuotes: the landing clearance shall include the designator of the landing runway.

sourceUnits.claimText: A HEAVY aircraft shall not be requested to land beyond the touchdown zone of a runway.
sourceUnits.rationale: Specific prohibition for HEAVY aircraft. Consistent across all attempts.
exactSourceQuotes: A HEAVY aircraft shall not be requested to land beyond the touchdown zone of a runway.

sourceUnits.rationale: Timing prohibition. Consistent across all attempts.

sourceUnits.rationale: Referential note. Consistent across all attempts.
exactSourceQuotes: Note 2.— Wake turbulence categories of aircraft and longitudinal separation minima are contained in Chapter 4, Section 4.9 and Chapter 5, Section 5.8, respectively.

sourceUnits.claimText: A landing aircraft will not normally be permitted to cross the runway threshold on its final approach until the preceding departing aircraft has crossed the end of the runway-in-use, has started a turn, or until all preceding landing aircraft are clear of the runway-in-use.
sourceUnits.rationale: Core separation prohibition in 7.10.1. Consistent across all attempts.
exactSourceQuotes: a landing aircraft will not normally be permitted to cross the runway threshold on its final approach until the preceding departing aircraft has crossed the end of the runway-in-use, or has started a turn, or until all preceding landing aircraft are clear of the runway-in-use.

sourceUnits.claimText: The report that a runway has been vacated shall be made when the entire aircraft is beyond the relevant runway-holding position.
sourceUnits.rationale: Vacate report timing definition. Consistent across all attempts.
exactSourceQuotes: The report shall be made when the entire aircraft is beyond the relevant runway-holding position.

sourceUnits.claimText: ATC clearances must be issued early enough to ensure that they are transmitted to the aircraft in sufficient time for it to comply with them.
sourceUnits.rationale: Specifies the timing requirement for issuing clearances.
exactSourceQuotes: ATC clearances must be issued early enough to ensure that they are transmitted to the aircraft in sufficient time for it to comply with them.

sourceUnits.claimText: When issuing a clearance covering a requested change in route or level, the exact nature of the change shall be included in the clearance.
sourceUnits.rationale: Requires explicit inclusion of the change details in amended clearances.
exactSourceQuotes: the exact nature of the change shall be included in the clearance.

sourceUnits.claimText: When prior coordination has been effected with units under whose control the aircraft will subsequently come, or if there is reasonable assurance that it can be effected a reasonable time prior to their assumption of control, the clearance limit shall be the destination aerodrome or, if not practicable, an appropriate intermediate point.
sourceUnits.rationale: Specifies the clearance limit when coordination with subsequent control units is established.
exactSourceQuotes: the clearance limit shall be the destination aerodrome or, if not practicable, an appropriate intermediate point

sourceUnits.claimText: Aircraft intending supersonic flight shall, whenever practicable, be cleared for the transonic acceleration phase prior to departure.
sourceUnits.rationale: Specifies the requirement for clearing supersonic aircraft for transonic acceleration before departure.
exactSourceQuotes: be cleared for the transonic acceleration phase prior to departure.

sourceUnits.claimText: If an air traffic control clearance is not suitable to the pilot-in-command of an aircraft, the flight crew may request and, if practicable, obtain an amended clearance.
sourceUnits.rationale: Establishes the pilot's right to request amended clearances.
exactSourceQuotes: the flight crew may request and, if practicable, obtain an amended clearance.

sourceUnits.claimText: When traffic conditions will not permit clearance of a requested change, the word 'UNABLE' shall be used.
sourceUnits.rationale: Mandates the use of 'UNABLE' when a requested change cannot be granted.
exactSourceQuotes:
When traffic conditions will not permit clearance of a requested change, the word “UNABLE” shall be
used.

sourceUnits.claimText: When a flight plan specifies that the initial portion of a flight will be uncontrolled, the aircraft shall be advised to obtain its clearance from the ATC unit in whose area controlled flight will be commenced.
sourceUnits.rationale: Defines the procedure for aircraft starting uncontrolled flight.
exactSourceQuotes: the aircraft shall be advised to obtain its clearance from the ATC unit in whose area controlled flight will be commenced.

sourceUnits.claimText: The route of flight shall be detailed in each clearance when deemed necessary.
sourceUnits.rationale: Mandates the detailing of the route in clearances when necessary.
exactSourceQuotes: The route of flight shall be detailed in each clearance when deemed necessary.

sourceUnits.claimText: When warranted by circumstances, an alternative route or level should be offered.
sourceUnits.rationale: Recommends offering an alternative when a change is denied.
exactSourceQuotes: an alternative route or level should be offered.

sourceUnits.claimText: If an aircraft has been cleared to an intermediate point in adjacent controlled airspace, the appropriate ATC unit will then be responsible for issuing, as soon as practicable, an amended clearance to the destination aerodrome.
sourceUnits.rationale: Assigns responsibility for issuing the final clearance to the destination when an intermediate point was previously cleared.
exactSourceQuotes: the appropriate ATC unit will then be responsible for issuing, as soon as practicable, an amended clearance to the destination aerodrome.

sourceUnits.claimText: When an aircraft files, at the departure aerodrome, flight plans for the various stages of flight through intermediate stops, the initial clearance limit will be the first destination aerodrome and new clearances shall be issued for each subsequent portion of flight.
sourceUnits.rationale: Defines the clearance limit and issuance process for flights with intermediate stops.
exactSourceQuotes: the initial clearance limit will be the first destination aerodrome and new clearances shall be issued for each subsequent portion of flight.

sourceUnits.claimText: The phrase 'cleared flight planned route' shall not be used when granting a re-clearance.
sourceUnits.rationale: Prohibits the use of 'cleared flight planned route' during re-clearances.
exactSourceQuotes: The phrase “cleared flight planned route” shall not be used when granting a re-clearance.

sourceUnits.claimText: Clearances shall, except as provided for in Chapter 6, Section 6.3.2, concerning standard departure clearances, contain the items specified in Chapter 11, 11.4.2.6.2.1.
sourceUnits.rationale: References the specific list of items required in clearances, excluding standard departures.
exactSourceQuotes: contain the items specified in Chapter 11, 11.4.2.6.2.1.

sourceUnits.claimText: By prior arrangement between ATC units and the operators, aircraft operating on an established schedule may, if the proposed route of flight is through more than one control area, be cleared through intermediate stops within other control areas but only after coordination between the ACCs concerned.
sourceUnits.rationale: Allows for clearance through intermediate stops under specific coordination conditions.
exactSourceQuotes: be cleared through intermediate stops within other control areas but only after coordination between the ACCs concerned.

sourceUnits.claimText: When so requested by the flight crew, an aircraft shall be cleared for cruise climb whenever traffic conditions and coordination procedures permit.
sourceUnits.rationale: Mandates the issuance of cruise climb clearances upon request when conditions allow.
exactSourceQuotes: an aircraft shall be cleared for cruise climb whenever traffic conditions and coordination procedures permit.

sourceUnits.claimText: See 6.3.2.3 pertaining to standard clearances for departing aircraft and 6.5.2.3 pertaining to standard clearances for arriving aircraft.
sourceUnits.rationale: This is a reference note pointing to other sections; it does not contain an independent operative requirement.
exactSourceQuotes: See 6.3.2.3 pertaining to standard clearances for departing aircraft and 6.5.2.3 pertaining to standard clearances for arriving aircraft.

sourceUnits.claimText: When a flight plan specifies that the first portion of a flight will be subject to ATC and the subsequent portion will be uncontrolled, the aircraft shall normally be cleared to the point at which the controlled flight terminates.
sourceUnits.rationale: Defines the clearance limit for flights transitioning from controlled to uncontrolled airspace.
exactSourceQuotes: the aircraft shall normally be cleared to the point at which the controlled flight terminates.

sourceUnits.claimText: The phrases 'cleared (designation) departure' or 'cleared (designation) arrival' may be used when standard departure or arrival routes have been established by the appropriate ATS authority and published in Aeronautical Information Publications (AIPs).
sourceUnits.rationale: Allows the use of standard departure/arrival route phrases when published.
exactSourceQuotes:
The phrases “cleared (designation) departure” or “cleared (designation) arrival” may be used when standard departure or
arrival routes have been established by the appropriate ATS authority and published in Aeronautical Information
Publications (AIPs).

sourceUnits.claimText: An ATC unit may request an adjacent ATC unit to clear aircraft to a specified point during a specified period.
sourceUnits.rationale: Allows for inter-unit requests for aircraft clearance.
exactSourceQuotes: An ATC unit may request an adjacent ATC unit to clear aircraft to a specified point during a specified period.

exactSourceQuotes: an aircraft should whenever possible be offered the most direct routing.

sourceUnits.claimText: Clearances are issued solely for expediting and separating air traffic and are based on known traffic conditions which affect safety in aircraft operation.
sourceUnits.rationale: Defines the fundamental scope and purpose of ATC clearances.
exactSourceQuotes: Clearances are issued solely for expediting and separating air traffic and are based on known traffic conditions which affect safety in aircraft operation.

sourceUnits.claimText: ATC units shall issue such ATC clearances as are necessary to prevent collisions and to expedite and maintain an orderly flow of air traffic.

exactSourceQuotes: ATC units shall issue such ATC clearances as are necessary to prevent collisions and to expedite and maintain an orderly flow of air traffic.

sourceUnits.rationale: Assigns responsibility for amended clearances and traffic information during en-route flight.
exactSourceQuotes: it will be the responsibility of the appropriate ATC unit to issue an amended clearance whenever necessary

sourceUnits.claimText: When an alternative route is offered and accepted by the flight crew under the procedures described in 4.5.7.4.2, the amended clearance issued shall describe the route to the point where it joins the previously cleared route, or, if the aircraft will not re-join the previous route, to the destination.

exactSourceQuotes: the amended clearance issued shall describe the route to the point where it joins the previously cleared route, or, if the aircraft will not re-join the previous route, to the destination.

exactSourceQuotes: A clearance limit shall be described by specifying the name of the appropriate significant point, or aerodrome, or controlled airspace boundary.

exactSourceQuotes:
The phrase “cleared flight planned route” may be used to describe any route or portion thereof, provided the route or portion thereof is identical to
that filed in the flight plan and sufficient routing details are given to definitely establish the aircraft on its route.

exactSourceQuotes: forward a clearance to approach control units or aerodrome control towers with the least possible delay
